en: I worship Rāmacandra, who is radiant with the knowledge that negates one's own ignorance, duality, and their effects, and who is to be known through the Mantropaniṣad.
Oṃ. That is fullness, this is fullness; from fullness, fullness arises.
When fullness is taken from fullness, fullness alone remains.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.
Oṃ! I am the eight-footed, pure swan, the subtle thread of the three-fold path, the imperishable;
beholding the light of that which has three paths everywhere, one does not see [anything else]. || 1 ||
When the time for the delusion of beings has come and the darkness of Vaikharī speech has been pierced,
those established in purity perceive the Attributeless within the thicket of the qualities.
It is impossible for those boys to perceive it otherwise while they meditate upon her—
the unborn, eternal, eightfold Prakṛti, who is ignorance and the source of all transformations.
By that [Prakṛti], [the world] is meditated upon—that is, presided over—and it is again stretched out and impelled;
and the world, presided over by that very same [Prakṛti], produces the objects of human purpose.
She is fair-complexioned, without beginning or end, the mother, the source of all beings; white, black, and red, she is the cow of plenty for the Lord.
Childish men drink this which is beyond the senses and incomprehensible;
but the one God alone drinks it here, acting according to His own will and subject to no other.
Through meditation and ritual action, the all-pervading Lord enjoys her, who yields nourishment common to all and is being drunk by the performers of sacrifice, even as he forcibly consumes her.
In this [Self], the great-souled ones perceive the golden eater of the fruit;
the Snātakas and Adhvaryus have sung of it as the indifferent, eternal Haṃsa.
The Bahvṛcas, experts in the scriptures, praise him as he is being praised;
the Rathantara and Bṛhat Sāmans are sung by those versed in the sevenfold Veda.

These descendants of Bhṛgu, the best of the Bhṛgus, who are masters of the Atharva Veda, recite the Brahman consisting of the secret essence of mantras, arranged according to the Pada and Krama methods.
The conduct toward fellow celibates, as well as the pillar and the one with fruit;
the ox, the Rohita fish, the remnant of food, and those seeing the great extent—thus [the verses]. 11.
He is Time and the Lord Vital Breath, Death, Śarva, Maheśvara, Ugra, Bhava, and Rudra, together with the gods and the asuras.
The omnipresent Lord is praised by means of hymns known through the Atharvaveda— hymns consisting of mantras— which celebrate Prajāpati, Virāṭ, Puruṣa, and the Waters themselves.
The Atharvaśiras knows that Puruṣa, who is devoid of qualities, as the twenty-sixth according to these [Sāṅkhya] teachers, and likewise as the twenty-seventh according to others.
That which is reckoned as twenty-fourfold, as well as the manifest and the unmanifest, they call non-dual, dual, threefold, and likewise fivefold. (15)
With the eye of knowledge, they behold everything from Brahmā down to the stationary beings;
the twice-born see that one alone, the utterly pure and all-pervading Lord.
In that very [Brahman] in which all this—Brahma, the moving and the unmoving—is woven, into that alone do they go to their dissolution, just as rivers [merge] into the ocean. 17.
In that [state] all entities dissolve, and having dissolved, they attain the state of the unmanifest;
then, seeing them once more as manifest, they are born again like bubbles.
And when presided over by the Knower of the Field (kṣetrajña), it exists again through causal factors;
thus do others behold that Blessed Lord again and again.
Those Brahmins who know it as "Brahman, Brahman" and approach it accordingly, they attain dissolution right here; once dissolved, they abide in the unmanifest.
"They are dissolved and characterized by the unmanifest," thus says the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ. That is fullness, this is fullness; from fullness, fullness arises.
When fullness is taken from fullness, only fullness remains.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.
Thus ends the Mantrikopaniṣad.
